🤝 Sponsors & Supporters

[!IMPORTANT] ANY.RUN lookups are read-only; case binary submissions are automatic when keyed. /cti downloads APK/installer links to cases/<case>/bin/, runs static analysis and, when ANYRUN_API_KEY is set in a spending run, submits each complete file through the private-by-default sandbox client. --free-only, case no_spend, default loop (unless --full) and hostile/no-direct-contact posture block submission; plan checks and privacy read-back still apply. A public-only account is refused unless ANYRUN_ALLOW_PUBLIC=1; public tasks are world-readable and irreversible. Direct anyrun_submit remains ask-first and requires HARNESS_ALLOW_SUBMIT=1. See SKILL.md.

Listing here reflects support for the project and does not imply affiliation, endorsement, or any verification of this tool by the organisations named. Integrations marked above are optional and key-gated — every core technique still runs with zero API keys. Always respect each provider's terms of service. The full list of open-source projects and free public-interest services this skill depends on is in Acknowledgments & Credits.



What is CTI Expert?

A Claude Code skill that transforms Claude into a trained cyber threat intelligence and open-source intelligence analyst. It runs structured intelligence collection using 120+ commands across 59 techniques — no API keys required for core functionality. To take full advantage, add your own free or paid API keys to the skill's .env — each is auto-detected and unlocks higher-tier access (e.g., Wigle, VirusTotal, URLScan.io, Shodan, Censys, SecurityTrails, WhoisXML).

[!TIP] Keyless by default, more powerful with your keys. Every core technique runs with zero API keys. Add any free or paid keys to .env (or run /apikeys set <service> <KEY>) and the skill auto-detects them, unlocking higher-tier pivots: reverse favicon→host, passive DNS, certificate search, sibling-domain discovery. A missing or bad key never breaks a run — it just degrades to a note. Setup guide: handbook/api-keys.md.

[!TIP] One skill, two layers. cti-expert is the broad collector — the wide net (/sweep, /webpivot, /subdomain, /username, /email-deep…). Built into the repo is a deep pipeline (intel_engine/) that turns raw collection into a real case: a persistent knowledge base, versioned cases, cross-case correlation, and calibrated assessment. The flow reads like a sentence — collect broadly → "seen this operator before?" → cluster → filter false positives → assess. No external setup: the backend resolves to SELF, and as of v2.9 the bundled installer (scripts/install.{sh,ps1}) provisions the deep layer automatically (or by hand: uv venv && uv pip install -r requirements.txt). Architecture: connectors/intel-backend.md.

Core Capability

Multi-vector reconnaissance on any target type — person, domain, organization, username, email, IP, WiFi — with automated finding validation, exposure scoring, and structured intelligence delivery.

AEAD Workflow

Acquire raw data → Enrich with pivot expansion → Assess findings → Deliver structured reports — the base bundle (Markdown + JSON + CSV + IOC bundle) always saves, then you pick a presentation report: PDF, DOCX, HTML, or all.


What's New — unreleased (next version)

The release that makes the analyst's judgement checkable. Published research and tradecraft become operating procedures with their limits written in, an identity claim now has to climb a ladder rung by rung, every capture a finding rests on carries a custody record, and the report gains the sections an organisation-risk engagement needs — risk by domain, supplier and partner exposure, threat events, and an honest list of what was checked and came back empty. New collectors stay passive: /suppliers reads the case's stored raws and /appliance-scan never contacts the target.

Category What's New Details
Research-grounded tradecraft 19 papers plus Heuer's Psychology of Intelligence Analysis rewritten as procedures in the modules that own the topic Each idea lands as trigger → steps → confounders → abstention; [Pxx …] text restates the source, (adaptation) marks how cti-expert applies it, and a number quoted from a paper describes that paper's dataset — never a threshold for a case. Lands in: ACH (8 steps) + bias checks B1–B10 in handbook/analytic-standards.md; Diamond events, activity threads/groups, Pyramid-of-Pain pivot priority and ATT&CK mapping limits in the new handbook/intrusion-modeling.md; passive-DNS maliciousness checks with confounders and the temporal pivot rule (co-resolution links only on overlapping windows) in fx-dns-cert-history.md §2.6–2.7; NXDOMAIN/DGA triage as a lead generator and botnet/C2 estate reconstruction from independent vantage points in domain-advanced.md; darknet measurement, review and alias-linkage limits; the on-chain evidence ladder. Older advice the sources contradict was corrected in the same pass — e.g. a shared username no longer reads as the same person (claim ladder), "IDENTITY CONFIRMED (87%)" became one likelihood term, Jaccard > 0.35 is no longer a "strong authorship link", a wallet counts as operator-grade only after it spends outside a service cluster, two domains on one IP mean shared infrastructure rather than co-ownership, and maliciously_registered is a leading hypothesis to corroborate, not "safe to cluster". Every source, its read status and where it landed: docs/research-sources.md. No paper's classifier is implemented
Identity claim ladder Same handle ≠ same person — four rungs, each with its own evidence bar username-osint.md §7: L1 string → L2 controller → L3 person → L4 named identity. A handle rarity grade (GENERIC / MODERATE / RARE — never a per-handle probability) now caps username-pivot priority in pivot_suggest (generic → low, rare → high; scripts/references/handle_rarity.json). The limits are written in: stylometry only ranks a stated candidate set, graph-topology linkage false-matches neighbours, and a pre-aged or resold account's history is not its current controller
Chain of custody Captures a finding rests on are hashed, sealed and logged Append-only, hash-chained cases/<case>/evidence/custody.jsonl (utc, action, actor, item, sha256, note, prev). /screenshot --verify / capture_evidence verify=true re-hash a capture against the first digest logged for it and seal it read-only (a mismatch is TAMPERED and never sealed); working_copy=true copies it to evidence/work/; fixity_sample=N [seed=S] re-hashes a random sample; manual hand-offs via wp_capture.py --custody transfer|export|cite, inside the case only. Outputs carry a custody_head (SHA256:COUNT): keep it elsewhere and check it with --check-log --expected-head to detect a cut or rewritten tail. Each screenshot records collector (a case-salted pseudonym unless CTI_COLLECTOR is set), persona, egress_ip, clock_sync and browser/tool versions. New handbook/collection-preservation.md, built on the Berkeley Protocol (OHCHR 2022): pre-collection risk check, per-item capture fields, three-part verification. An ad-hoc --outdir capture outside the case store has no custody log and is not sealed
STIX 2.1 conformance · TLP 2.0 The IOC bundle follows the OASIS spec; every label is FIRST TLP 2.0 The STIX exporter (generate-cti-iocs.py) emits SCO UUIDv5 ids, millisecond Z timestamps, the indicator required fields, resolvable refs and the official TLP 2.0 marking ids (checked by a local conformance test). TLP 2.0 everywhere — IntelReport, /report, /misp-export, the STIX markings: clear · green · amber · amber+strict (recipient organisation only) · red; CLEAR replaces WHITE. The STIX and MISP marking is the most restrictive one across the case fields, bare or TLP:-prefixed; an unreadable marking stops the export unless --tlp sets it, a RED case needs --allow-red, and an explicit --tlp looser than the case marking needs --allow-downgrade (and still warns)
Relationship card maps Who the subject is connected to, as a hub-and-panel figure Subject at the top, grouped panels of cards — name, role, dates, country-code chip, relation chip, Admiralty badge; dashed = claim not confirmed. The house report draws a person map (subject_profile + relationships rows), a threat-landscape map (actors, grouped by type) and a suppliers map (cases/<id>/suppliers.json) — only when that data exists — and the maps also ship in REPORT.json / HTML / DOCX. Card text passes the report's scrub/masking, and e-mail, phone and birth-date patterns are stripped from cards (pattern-based, not guaranteed anonymisation); --mask reduces person names to initials. Standalone: card_map.py spec.json -o map.svg --png map.png [--mask]
Organisation risk by domain /exposure --model organisation — ten domains, each rated by the analyst affiliates · impersonation · edge · insider · personnel · actors · credentials · suppliers · mail_dns · code_docs, each exploitability 0–3 × harm 0–3 (rationale required at harm 3) → domain score 0–10; overall = mean of rated domains, Critical ≥8 · High ≥6 · Medium ≥4 · Low, P1 7d / P2 30d / P3 90d. Unrated domains are listed as coverage gaps (warning below half) and never compared across coverage. --case writes cases/<id>/exposure_organisation.json, the report's risk_assessment (overall risk in the Executive Summary, rating scales in Methodology, exposure charts in Findings). Analyst judgement, not a probability
New report sections /report-sections carries the organisation, threat and person blocks Each renders only when present: key_findings {n, finding, severity, priority} in the Executive Summary; partner exposure — affiliate_exposure {org, country, infected_hosts, latest_infection, stealer_family, portal} and leak_claims with a "K of N proven" tally; threat_events {event, start, end, location, why_it_raises_risk, local_legal_notes, grade}; email_services {email, service, evidence, date} in Findings; usernames_to_reserve {platform, handle, available|taken_by_other|reserved} in Recommendations; negative_checks as "Checked — nothing found" in Sources checked
Supplier exposure /suppliers — the subject's supplier map from what the case already collected TXT verification tokens, SPF includes, MX, NS, CNAME chains (artifacts.cnames from wp_recon.detect_cnames on the collected host, plus guessed www/sso/mail/status under an apex on organisation cases only — those probes are visible to the target's authoritative DNS), cert issuer and same-site document metadata → cases/<id>/suppliers.json (high/medium/low). Then per-supplier breach / KEV / stealer checks and the suppliers card map. A supplier is a relationship of the subject, never an operator link; --kb writes facts only. Technique: techniques/fx-supplier-exposure.md
/appliance-scan Passive edge/VPN appliance scan — the target is never contacted Shodan InternetDB keyless and first; Shodan host / Censys when keyed, only for IPs where InternetDB showed a catalogue product, port or tag, at most 4 IPs, planned credits printed before spending (skipped under --free-only or scope no_spend, metered calls ledgered). Citrix/F5/Cisco ASA+Expressway/Ivanti/FortiGate/PAN-OS/Exchange and peers from CPEs and stored banners → CISA KEV family matches → patch lag in days after a verified advisory (rows without a source URL are ignored; --advisory supplies your own), plus index uptime → "no reboot since" with the 497.1-day wrap caveat. CRITICAL only when the analyst confirms the version (--version-confirmed) and a verified advisory puts it below the fix for a KEV CVE; a CPE- or index-read version stays TENTATIVE, and a branch-only version (13.1 vs fix 13.1.49.15) is branch_only, never pre-fix. Never says "vulnerable"; not auto-run by /case; --case writes cases/<id>/appliances.json
Evaluation hygiene · judgement fixtures Any claim that something works needs an evaluation card docs/evaluation-hygiene.md: the ten ML-in-security pitfalls (Arp et al.) become rules — temporal split, stated base rate, baselines; no card → the claim is an untested heuristic, and "not evaluated" beats a number. From CTIBench: a benchmark score ≠ case accuracy, evidence-span citation, abstention as a scored outcome. Five synthetic judgement fixtures (span-required TTPs, masked-actor abstention, shared infra ≠ operator, temporal holdout, CVSS computed by code from the vector) scored by claim_scorer.py — local-only, not shipped in the repository
Actor Threat Score /exposure --model actor — one actor against one organisation, 0–1 intent / capability / sectoral_reach / org_exposure in 0.25 steps, each with a rationale (intent ≥ 0.75 must cite evidence); Opportunity = 0.6·reach + 0.4·exposure; Score = 0.5·I + 0.25·C + 0.25·O; Intent floor rule (I = 0 → 0). Bands Critical ≥ 0.85 / High ≥ 0.60 / Medium ≥ 0.35 / Low ≥ 0.10 / Negligible (needs a written rationale), each with a standing posture and review date. --case keeps cases/<id>/actor_scores.json with re-score history (a shift > 0.10 without a reason is flagged). An organisation-specific lead, never attribution; analyst judgement, not a probability. Adapted from the MIT-licensed Packt companion repository Advanced Cyber Threat Intelligence and Hunting (2026) — see docs/research-sources.md
Severity Tier Matrix /exposure --model tier — threat severity × exposure → P1–P4 P1 7d / P2 30d / P3 90d / P4 track only; P1 needs both axes and nothing auto-closes. --case + item= keeps cases/<id>/tier_log.json, and a re-tier must name its trigger. Key findings accept P4 ("track only — no deadline"); the roadmap stays P1–P3. Rules in handbook/severity-tiers.md and analysis/weight-engine.md §10 (same Packt companion repo)
Emerging-threat response workflow A CVE, vendor advisory, campaign, actor profile or supply-chain trigger, answered for a defended organisation workflows/wf-emerging-threat.md: Admiralty-graded intake, Axis 1 → provisional tier, five-dimension exposure (passive vs consumer-owned), Axis 1 × Axis 2 tier (/exposure --model tier --case), Threat Advisory then the house-report Threat Assessment, a hunt package, acknowledgments in cases/<id>/distribution.jsonl, +7/+30-day re-runs (same Packt companion repo)
Actor threat-profile report One Actor Profile chapter after Findings — in the house report, REPORT.json, HTML and DOCX, in the same order actor_profile in the report block (name, aliases, attribution {assessment, likelihood term, confidence, dissent}, activity timeline, intent, capability, victimology, persona/OPSEC, tempo summary) plus claim_confidence, pivot_opportunities, a playbook row per ATT&CK tactic, hunt_hypotheses (HH-nn) and telemetry_priorities, with a derived ATT&CK coverage table. Attribution always prints its ICD-203 likelihood term and confidence, and every dissent line is shown. The Threat Score is read only from actor_scores.json — a lead, never attribution. Lint flags attribution without likelihood or confidence, intent without evidence, a High claim without sources, a hunt hypothesis without telemetry, a playbook ATT&CK id without evidence and a Critical key finding at P4. Synthetic example: handbook/report-template.md
Operator tempo case_timeline --tempo — when the operator works, as a lead only operator_tempo in the evidence ledger: an hour × weekday UTC histogram of operator-chosen timestamps only (non-bot commit author times, operator post/message/panel events, manually issued certs, registrations — ACME certs, crawls, scans, observation windows and date-only stamps are dropped with a reason), the UTC offsets whose local Mon–Fri 09:00–18:00 window holds most events, a second-rhythm flag, insufficient below 30 events / 10 distinct days, and its confounders. Never feeds attribution, clustering or KB edges ("consistent with UTC+N business hours — lead"; handbook/intrusion-modeling.md §10)
Hunt-package library 67 published hunting queries, linked, never copied, for a consumer who holds telemetry intel_engine/IntelAnalysis/references/hunt_packages.json indexes the Packt companion repo's ES|QL / EQL / KQL / Sigma / SPL queries, pinned to one commit, in 13 ATT&CK tactic groups — each with an ABLE hypothesis, CAR-style telemetry, prerequisites, method and false-positive notes. Pick by ATT&CK id → tactic → the consumer's telemetry; every query is validated in the consumer's environment against their own baselines, and cti-expert never runs them. Includes the Time-Terrain-Behavior diversity score and its velocity extension for machine-speed activity. Procedure: workflows/wf-threat-analyst.md Phase 5
REA 6.9.0 The deep-static binary layer moves its pin from 6.7.0 to 6.9.0 /binary runs REA by default (static commands only; rea-agents@6.9.0 installed by hand, Node ^22.23.4 / ^24.22.1 / >=26.12.1; --no-rea / rea=false skips). Go binaries (PE, ELF, Mach-O) now also yield their embedded string literals (inspect-go-binary --include-string-literals, capped at 2000, cited go string @<file offset>) into the IOC sweep, so URLs compiled into a Go build become leads; a dotted literal counts only with a scheme, @, host/path or ip:port, so Go runtime names are not read as hosts. REA 6.9.0's new error format (only code/category, no result, exit 1) is reported as an error instead of being misread as a successful run
Yamato Security hunt handoff A second link-only hunt index for a consumer who holds Windows or cloud logs intel_engine/IntelAnalysis/references/hunt_rules_yamato.json maps 389 ATT&CK techniques to Yamato Security's Sigma rules — hayabusa-rules (Windows event logs) and suzaku-rules (AWS / Azure / M365 / Google Workspace), both DRL 1.1 with each rule's author kept on any shared rule or reported match — plus 187 Senrigan hunts (AGPL-3.0: CloudTrail, Suzaku-timeline, VPC Flow Log). Every document of a Sigma correlation file is indexed and is a valid hunt_package_ref. Titles and metadata only — no detection logic. The consumer runs Hayabusa / Takajō, Suzaku or Senrigan on their own logs; cti-expert never bundles or runs them
Windows logging baseline "Does the consumer even log this?" — answered before any hunt intel_engine/IntelAnalysis/references/telemetry_baselines.json maps each telemetry need to its Windows audit subcategory, the Windows default, what the Yamato, Microsoft and ASD baselines set, and the minimum log size — adapted from Yamato Security's EventLog-Baseline-Guide (MIT, pinned). Actor-profile telemetry_priorities rows may carry baseline_ref, printed as "— Windows audit setting: ()" in every report output; an unresolved ref is a lint warning, never a failure. The emerging-threat workflow (wf-emerging-threat.md §2, §3.4) starts its detection-exposure check with this question
What's New in v2.12

What's New in v2.12

The release where the premium keys start pulling their weight — and the report writes itself. v2.11 shipped detectors. v2.12 turns an eight-finding audit of the paid vendors into behaviour (every metered leg gated, bought once per case instead of once per host), adds Netlas as an independent index, makes the editorial PDF/DOCX a deterministic composition from the case directory, and closes the last honesty gap in the ANY.RUN docs: detonation exists, and it is gated five ways.

Category What's New Details
Cross-type auto-pivot loop Every selector type is a frontier node; /cti auto-approves metered spend by default (--review restores the per-round digest-bound approval) Typed nodes (selector_types + rungs.json owner/kit/neighbour) → case_state.propose → required Plan phase (PLAN_TOOLS, read-only) → auto free/urlscan pivots with ≤ N=25 hits, else proposal.json gated in audit.gate — auto-approved in AUTO mode (approved_by: auto in proposal.json + ledger; engage_account · webamon_scan · misp_publish · misp_push never), or harness approve · case_approve · TTY under --review. Dispatcher ops propose + corpus-search (corpus_search tool). Assessment gains additive kit_siblings / neighbours / mentions — collected, never attributed. Rail: collecting ≠ attributing
MO-neighbour pivot Reverse a non-CDN origin to its co-tenants — and only ever seed on a registrant join key wp_mo_neighbours.discover reverses the estate's non-CDN origin IP (also the MX origin) through Netlas · Validin · urlscan, WHOIS-verifies each candidate apex, and classifies it same_registrant (current registrant e-mail/phone join key only — a proxied record contributes no phone) / same_mo (reference-data policy) / unrelated / unverifiable. Only same_registrant seeds the frontier; same-MO personas render as a rung-10 Related personas table in the report (--mask-personas to aggregate). A bulk-hosting guard fires before any spend; per-origin lock + disk cache + a per-run WhoisXML ledger hold across collector subprocesses, so an origin is bought once per case. RULE 5 rails intact: facts-only KB ingest, never an edge, never an operator_lead
WHOIS eras · urlscan Pro lifecycle The timeline now knows who held the name before this operator WHOIS history is an explicit --whois-history purchase scoped to seeds and cluster members (the render path never buys it); the house report renders a Registrant eras table (same-day flaps folded, registrar placeholders classed) and uses the current era's start as the archive-capture cutoff. urlscan Pro supplies the hostname lifecycle index — A/NS eras, CT and zonefile firsts, left-censored on a truncated walk — feeding the temporal view; verdict rows appear only on signal, and the API key is sent to urlscan.io only
Entitlement measured, not assumed A key measured free skips the calls that would 403 wp_capabilities.discover_plans probes each vendor's free account endpoint (urlscan quotas, Netlas plan, SecurityTrails/DNSLytics usage, IntelX /authenticate/info, Validin /api/paths) once per case into cases/<id>/capability_plans.json; enrich_live reads the store and gates only on a positive free verdict — unknown keeps the productive call as the probe. Censys search records its own verdict. A failed probe is reported this run and never frozen, so the next process re-measures
Netlas + the rest of the vendor wiring Every registered key now has a pivot behind it wp_netlas.py — Bearer client over the domains · responses · whois_domains · whois_ip · certs collections (search, count, facet, reverse-IP, plan), keyless query builder + web-UI links, ledgered, Cloudflare-safe UA; intel.py netlas ip|ns|spf|domain|san|title|plan|raw. Live-measured: domains a:<origin> returned 32 apexes on a 32-domain estate (15 members + same-MO siblings under other personas). Alongside: SecurityTrails DNS-history eras + DSL reverse-WHOIS (diffed against WhoisXML), DNSLytics reverse-IP under its own co-tenancy-routed key, GrayHatWarfare exposure lead + report section, Shodan cert/JARM search, once-per-case Censys cert search with a shared-cert fan-out guard, IntelX auto-fire in pipeline open (loop: --full only; role mailboxes excluded), and Validin wired natively (domain lookup, reputation, cert and favicon hosts). Frontier ranks owner-link candidates above lookalikes
The house report, composed deterministically The editorial PDF/DOCX no longer needs a model to write it intel.py house-report <CASE-ID> composes the IntelReport document from the case dir: sections I–XI, both confidence scales + the ICD-203 × Admiralty scatter, relationship graph + entity-relationship map, attribution inference chain, temporal view + registration heatmap + domain × shared-indicator matrix (which honours the §2.5 false-positive control and carries the WHOIS join keys), a landing-page capture per estate host (proxy-gated egress; a page that will not render falls back to the newest public web-scan, then a web-archive snapshot — captioned, dated by the archive, and labelled a previous owner's page when it predates the current registration), per-domain dossiers, a glossary, Appendices A–E. Rule 12 scrub of tool/vendor/path names; third parties masked through one gate (scripts/cti_third_party_mask.py). One figure source (scripts/cti_report_figures.py
